title: Procedure for Consulting Authorities of Intended Receiving Countries before Proceeding with Deportations of Foreigners Convicted of Offences in Singapore
what_it_is: Procedure for Consulting Authorities of Intended Receiving Countries before Proceeding with Deportations of Foreigners Convicted of Offences in Singapore

sections.label: No standard deportation consultation protocol
sections.summary: There is no standard protocol of consulting receiving countries before deporting foreigners, and specific discussions are not disclosed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: As regards whether the Government has a standard protocol of consulting the authorities of the intended receiving countries before proceeding with the deportations of foreigners, the short answer is that there is no such standard protocol.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: As stated in my Ministry's reply on 2 July 2024, foreigners who are being deported can leave for any country to which their passports allow them to go.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The way we treat these persons is no different from any other traveller.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We do not consult the foreign countries beforehand as a general rule as to whether a traveller is allowed to go there.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: As regards Ms Lim's second specific question, the general position is that we do not disclose specific discussions.

sections.label: Deportees go where passports allow
sections.summary: The law lets deportees go where their passports allow, and what happens to them in the receiving country is legally irrelevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The law allows them to go where their passports allow them to go to.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, what we think about what will happen to them in the receiving country, whether it will be more favourable or less favourable, as Ms Lim will appreciate, is legally irrelevant and is not something that the Government can take into account.

sections.label: Interest and FATF chairmanship
sections.summary: The Government is interested and chairs the Financial Action Task Force.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Second, of course we are interested, which is why we are the chair of the Financial Action Task Force.

sections.label: Amended legislation on deportee destination
sections.summary: Amended legislation, once operationalised, will let the Government decide where to send a deportee, not based on views of legal systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We should not be making those value judgments.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: However, rather than engage in this back and forth, Ms Sylvia Lim may be aware that we have amended our legislation last year such that once it is operationalised, which should be sometime later this year or next year, the law will allow us to decide where to send such a deportee.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But the only consideration cannot be what we think of the different legal systems.
